name: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement

summary.text: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is the Department of Homeland Security agency responsible for interior immigration enforcement. In April 2025 ICE awarded Palantir Technologies a roughly $30 million sole-source task to build an 'Immigration Lifecycle Operating System' (ImmigrationOS) on top of its existing Palantir-built Investigative Case Management platform, citing urgency and a September 2025 prototype deadline; the task was renewed in September 2025, bringing the total to about $60 million.

facts.claim: ICE awarded Palantir a contract valued at about $30 million on April 11, 2025 to build an 'Immigration Lifecycle Operating System' (ImmigrationOS).
facts.quote: ICE awarded Palantir a $30 million contract on April 11 to build an "Immigration Lifecycle Operating System," or Immigration OS for short.

sources.title: ICE enlists Palantir to develop all-seeing 'ImmigrationOS' eye to speed up deportations

facts.claim: ICE's justification said the award had to be made without competition because the agency wanted a prototype ready by September 25, 2025 and argued Palantir was the only firm able to meet the timeline.
facts.quote: the deal had to be awarded quickly, with no opportunity for competing bids, because the immigration agency wants a prototype ready by September 25

facts.claim: ICE renewed the ImmigrationOS task on September 25, 2025, bringing its total value to about $60 million; the renewal's procurement listing shows a base-and-options value of $29,898,236 issued under a limited-source justification.
facts.quote: ICE renewed the contract on Sept. 25, bringing its total value to about $60 million.
